title: What are JPA entity lifecycle callbacks and when does each one fire?
keyPoints: @PrePersist fires before INSERT and is used to set defaults like creation timestamps and reference numbers.
@PostPersist fires after INSERT when the generated ID is available, ideal for publishing domain events.
@PreUpdate fires before UPDATE only if dirty checking detects actual changes to the entity.
@PreRemove fires before DELETE for cleanup, logging, or soft-delete interception.
@PostLoad fires after an entity is loaded from the database, ideal for computing @Transient derived fields.
Callbacks must not call EntityManager operations (no queries, no flush) to avoid recursion.
For cross-cutting logic across entities, use a shared listener class registered with @EntityListeners.

s1_definition.oneliner: JPA lifecycle callbacks are annotated methods that fire automatically around INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, and LOAD operations without any manual invocation.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **@PrePersist** -- fires before the INSERT is flushed, used to set creation defaults like timestamps and reference numbers.
- **@PostPersist** -- fires after the INSERT when the generated ID is available, used for event publishing and logging.
- **@PreUpdate** -- fires before an UPDATE is flushed, only if Hibernate's dirty checking detected actual changes.
- **@PostUpdate** -- fires after the UPDATE completes.
- **@PreRemove** -- fires before the DELETE is flushed, used for cleanup, audit logging, or soft-delete interception.
- **@PostRemove** -- fires after the DELETE completes.
- **@PostLoad** -- fires after an entity is loaded from the database, used for computing @Transient derived fields.
- **@EntityListeners** -- registers external listener classes for cross-cutting callback logic shared across entities.
s1_definition.analogy: At National Bank of India, lifecycle callbacks are automatic stamps the system puts on a form at each stage. @PrePersist is the stamp right before a new account form is filed: "set the open date, generate the reference number." @PostPersist is the confirmation stamp after filing: "send the welcome SMS." @PreUpdate stamps just before edits are saved: "record the modification time." @PreRemove stamps before a file is archived: "mark as closed, notify compliance." @PostLoad is what happens the moment a clerk pulls a file from the cabinet: "compute the display balance." Nobody tells the clerk each time; these happen automatically.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Entity Lifecycle Callbacks:

  ┌──────────┐   @PrePersist   ┌────────┐   @PostPersist   ┌──────────┐
  │ Transient │ ──────────────> │ INSERT │ ──────────────> │ Managed  │
  │ (new)     │  set defaults   │  SQL   │  log / event    │          │
  └──────────┘                 └────────┘                 └──────────┘
       │                                                       │
       │                                                       │
       │         @PostLoad                                     │
       │  <────────────────  (on find / query)                 │
       │   compute @Transient                                  │
       │                                                       │
       │                    @PreUpdate    ┌────────┐   @PostUpdate
       │                  ──────────────> │ UPDATE │ ──────────────>
       │                   set updatedAt  │  SQL   │   log / event
       │                                 └────────┘
       │
       │                    @PreRemove    ┌────────┐   @PostRemove
       │                  ──────────────> │ DELETE │ ──────────────>
       │                   audit / check  │  SQL   │   cleanup
       │                                 └────────┘

  Firing order with @EntityListeners:
  ┌──────────────┐    ┌──────────────┐
  │ Listener     │ -> │ Entity       │
  │ callback     │    │ callback     │
  │ (fires FIRST)│    │ (fires SECOND)│
  └──────────────┘    └──────────────┘
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
JPA lifecycle callbacks are automatic hooks that fire at well-defined points in an entity's persistence lifecycle, removing the need to remember to call them from service code. @PrePersist runs before the insert and is where you set creation timestamps and generate reference numbers. @PostPersist runs after the insert when the generated ID exists, making it ideal for logging or publishing domain events. @PreUpdate runs before an update but only if Hibernate's dirty checking detected an actual change.

@PostLoad is the callback developers most often forget. It runs immediately after an entity is loaded from the database, making it the correct place to compute derived @Transient fields like available balance (balance minus hold amount) or full name (first name plus last name). In our National Bank of India transaction service, @PrePersist guarantees every transaction gets a creation timestamp and a unique TXN reference before insertion, eliminating a whole class of bugs where developers forgot to set those fields.

For cross-cutting logic that applies across many entities, move the callback methods into a shared listener class registered with @EntityListeners. The listener's callbacks fire before the entity's own callbacks, providing a clean separation between generic audit logging and entity-specific initialization. The critical rule is that callbacks must stay lightweight and must never call EntityManager to run queries or force a flush, because that can cause recursion inside the flush cycle.

Remember one sentence: lifecycle callbacks fire automatically around INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, and LOAD so you never forget to set defaults, stamp timestamps, or compute derived fields, but keep them lightweight and never call EntityManager from within them.
